Bitcoin stabilized near the $64,000–$64,200 threshold midday June 21, executing a muted 1.3% technical bounce despite persistent extreme fear sentiment. The primary headwind remains a historic institutional exodus; U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs have recorded a staggering $6.35 billion in net outflows over the trailing 30 days, marking six consecutive weeks of structural withdrawals as asset managers reduce risk exposures.

Conversely, derivatives infrastructure is maturing. Kraken successfully launched the first CFTC-regulated crypto perpetual futures contracts for U.S. clients via Bitnomial, securing a critical regulated foothold for institutional hedging against spot volatility.

This defensive digital asset positioning is intrinsically linked to the Federal Reserve’s hawkish tightening under Chair Kevin Warsh. With the 10-year Treasury yield anchored near 4.46% and an aggressively repriced short end, elevated risk-free rates continue to siphon liquidity. Until this yield-curve pressure abates or the dollar weakens, crypto multiples will remain severely suppressed relative to resilient tech equities.
